trusted_bootstrap: Before a signed root has any operation, bind its existing domain/recipient to an immutable registered route context and TTL. Several roots may share a context only in the same tenant/domain. Not a new public route-management endpoint.
transaction_order: existing advance guarded transaction and current authority fence
public command and fixed work slot
optional L2 full result plus all charges
for every newly published job: public-policy WITHHELD or L3 ticket/request/outbox allocation using guarded transaction core
persist one public decision with the same domain job sequence and tick
invariants: Every published job has exactly one pub_decisions row, and every decision points to that published job/sequence/tick.
ADMITTED binds exactly one immutable route, L3 ticket, stable request key, original operation, and outbox; all outboxes are covered by admitted decisions.

WITHHELD has no ticket and no outbox. Public authorization/cancel or revoked route may cause withholding; unknown internal failures roll back rather than being converted to a public success/failure bit.
Result commit, all charges, publication eligibility, decision, ticket/outbox and tick retry mapping are atomic at the scheduler transaction boundary.
A witness-ahead/local-behind replica cannot advance until exact recovery; recovery does not republish, reclassify, resample or re-admit.
Separate admit_v2 is disabled in the new profile. Internal admission core requires a guarded transaction with sampled transaction clock and witness base anchor.
Recovery validates contribution source pairs, retention-v2 evidence/frontiers and public decision/ticket coverage before commit.

withholding_cases.cancel_before_L1: Original work retained; CANCELED budget returned; one WITHHELD decision at scheduled publication; no ticket.
withholding_cases.cancel_or_revoke_after_L1: Original work and no-refund semantics retained; withheld result is not eligible for a new delivery.
withholding_cases.route_revoked_before_publication: Internal kernel eligibility may be RELEASE, but final public decision WITHHELD and no ticket; the two records have different roles.
withholding_cases.action_expired: Scheduled authorization check yields WITHHELD; no later separate L3 call needed.
withholding_cases.credential_revoked_after_admission: Original bounded ticket may recover under unchanged retention semantics; cannot create new L3 through disabled API.
withholding_cases.unknown_storage_or_integrity_failure: Abort entire business transition; do not substitute WITHHELD. External error/availability observation still requires OBS-4.

schema.pub_decisions: one kind/delivery pointer per domain job sequence with original tick; not a signed public event feed

shared_core_change: Extracted existing retention-v2 admission checks and mutations into _admit_v2_tx. Existing admit_v2 remains a guarded wrapper with same authorization and fresh/retry distinction. No nested transaction or witness commit in core.

network.scope: Atomic count publication and fresh restore over actual loopback authenticated witness; no new public gateway or network result receiver.

verification.crash_scope: Eight ADMITTED and two WITHHELD local-reference process cuts. Separately, actual loopback TLS witness for atomic count publication and fresh restore. Not cross-host or power-loss testing.
verification.mixed_scope: Actual encrypted signed B4 N3 histogram plus count share final publication transaction in local reference profile.
verification.receiver_scope: Existing recipient accepts a new-profile original count ticket after intermediate-credential revocation; this case uses direct local recipient calls.

remaining: OBS-1 authenticated external public request/control/response gateway
OBS-3 domain-wide final frontier and cross-route transmission gate, including ordered WITHHELD events
OBS-4 exhaustive error/health/timeout mapping and private-failure observation proof
OBS-5 recovery for the still-unimplemented gateway/final-frontier state
OBS-6 physical observation and fault-process refinement
Public signed decision schema and independent interoperability
Actual workload identity/classifier/global lineage and production authority/key lifecycle
